field.note: k = F_13[a]/(a^6 - a^5 - 3a^4 - 3a^3 + a^2 + 5a + 4), the reduction of the Petri sextic

serialization_convention.element_lists: DESCENDING in a  (v = [c5,c4,c3,c2,c1,c0] means c5 a^5 + ... + c0)
serialization_convention.evidence: only this convention makes disc_u(H) = (t-lambda)^8 * (squares); the other three give 154 simple ramification points, impossible for a 3-branch-point cover

passport_from_the_model.reading: the only odd-multiplicity factor is (t-lambda)^8; every other factor has even multiplicity and is an index^2 contribution of the non-maximal order, not ramification
passport_from_the_model.different_degree: 8 (at lambda) + 22 (at the place P1, e=23) + 22 (at infinity) = 52 = 2g-2 + 2*23 with g = 4

fibre_at_lambda: q7 * d8^2 exactly (verified as a polynomial identity)

pole_structure_of_the_sheet_coordinate.at_infinity: u is a unit (all deg_t c_i = 0, two are -1)
pole_structure_of_the_sheet_coordinate.place_P1_degree_1: Newton hull [[0,-1],[23,0]]: all 23 roots have v(u) = -1/23; P1 is totally ramified, e = 23
pole_structure_of_the_sheet_coordinate.place_P2_degree_1: hull [[0,-1],[22,-1],[23,0]]: 22 roots units, ONE root with v(u) = -1
pole_structure_of_the_sheet_coordinate.place_P3_degree_2: same shape: 22 roots units, ONE root with v(u) = -1
pole_structure_of_the_sheet_coordinate.consequence: the P2/P3 poles are what blow up every resolvent degree bound: only 1 of 23 roots has the pole, so a heptad sum can have a pole of order 1 there and e_i(theta) a pole of order min(i,77) -- versus floor(i/23) if the poles sat only over P1
pole_structure_of_the_sheet_coordinate.fix: re-serialize the sheet polynomial with a Riemann-Roch generator of L(mQ), Q the point over P1: then deg_t c_i <= floor(m*i/23), which is the slope m/23 the chain already assumes (m = 4 gives 5820 unknowns)
